title: What to Do When Conversion Fails
description: Troubleshoot common conversion failures with practical checks that help you identify file issues, browser problems, and format mismatches.
author: Converigo

sections.title: Check the source file
sections.content: A damaged, encrypted, or oversized file can stop conversion before it starts. Verify that the file opens normally and is not protected by unusual restrictions.

sections.title: Verify format support
sections.content: Some converters support certain source and target combinations better than others. Confirm that the file type and output target are compatible with your chosen workflow.

sections.title: Retry with a clean browser session
sections.content: Browser caching and temporary storage issues can interfere with processing. A fresh session or a simple retry often resolves transient failures.

faq.question: What is the first thing I should check?
faq.answer: Verify that the uploaded file opens normally and is not corrupted, locked, or protected.

faq.question: Can unsupported formats cause failure?
faq.answer: Yes. If the source or target format is not supported by the selected converter, the process may fail.

faq.question: Should I retry immediately?
faq.answer: Sometimes, but it is also useful to confirm the file itself is valid before trying again.

call_to_action.text: Need help getting a conversion to work?
